ai.title: main-prompt.ts verification instruction requires knowledge file
ai.summary: backend/src/main-prompt.ts updated to conditionally require knowledge file commands for type/linter checks. Agent must only run <run_terminal_command> for verification if knowledge files specify a command, otherwise use <await_tool_results>. Internal prompt logic change.

eli5.text: The assistant is now told to only run a type-checker or linter command on its own if the project's own documentation files specify exactly which command to run; if those documentation files don't name a command, the assistant will wait for the results of its code changes instead of guessing what to run. If you watched the assistant working, you'd notice it no longer runs a check command automatically after making edits, and instead either runs a specific command named in the documentation or simply waits for feedback before moving on. This only affects the internal helper that guides the assistant's verification step, so the change is live now but is felt only by anyone building on top of this assistant tooling.

ai.title: Reduce prompt pressure for awaittoolresults
ai.summary: System prompts and tool descriptions updated to discourage simultaneous use of `await_tool_results` and `run_terminal_command`. The `agent-instructions.md` section explicitly mandating periodic `await_tool_results` was removed. This clarifies that verification via terminal commands is preferred, reserving `await_tool_results` for when no specific check command exists.

eli5.text: The assistant is now encouraged to check its work by running a project-specific command instead of always using a generic check-the-result tool. If you watched it work, you'd see it less often pause with the generic result-request tool when a clear command (like a type checker) is available, reserving that tool for cases with no specific check command. This guidance tweak is live in internal backend files today.

ai.title: Restrict Gemini thinking to max cost mode
ai.summary: Gemini thinking is now gated to `costMode === 'max'` instead of `!== 'lite'` in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`. This prevents thinking tokens from being generated in standard modes, reducing latency and cost for non-max requests.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to do something, it can spend extra effort thinking through a solution before replying. That extra thinking now only happens when you are on the most expensive pricing tier, not on the cheaper or standard tiers. So if it feels like the assistant is taking a bit longer to respond, it is because you are being charged at the highest rate and the assistant is doing more behind-the-scenes work. If you are on any other tier, that deeper thinking is skipped, and your responses come back faster and cost less.

ai.title: main-prompt.ts: enforce full paths for writefile and readfiles
ai.summary: main-prompt.ts strengthened the full-path instruction for write_file and read_files, adding 'Important:' prefix and explicit root-relative path requirement. Updated to warn about import path mismatches (e.g., backend/utils/foo.ts vs actual backend/src/utils/foo.ts). Scoped to Gemini Flash and Pro models only. Single backend/src/main-prompt.ts file changed.

eli5.text: The assistant now gets more specific instructions to always write down the complete location of a file when it talks about creating or reading one. If you asked it to look at a file, you'd notice it spells out the full path from the main project folder, like backend/src/utils/foo.ts instead of just utils/foo.ts, and it'll even remind you that sometimes the name it imports doesn’t match the real folder structure. This only changes how one type of internal helper talks, so regular users won’t see anything different in their daily work.

ai.title: Add training file context capture
ai.summary: New requestRelevantFilesForTraining function in backend/src/find-files/request-files-prompt.ts captures expanded file context for model training. Main prompt handler triggers asynchronous upload via uploadExpandedFileContextForTraining in backend/src/main-prompt.ts, logging errors without blocking. BigQuery schema updated in packages/bigquery/src/schema.ts with new trace types for file context and blobs.

eli5.text: When the assistant reviews the files relevant to your request, it now also quietly saves a broader, higher-quality snapshot of that file context to a secure data store, purely to help train a smarter version of the assistant later. You will not see anything different in your experience, the extra step runs in the background after each conversation, and if it ever fails, your chat keeps going without interruption. The data it collects is tagged separately from your conversation logs and only contains the file content the assistant already used, nothing private beyond what you shared in this session.

ai.title: Re-land training file context capture
ai.summary: Reverts previous revert, restoring `requestRelevantFilesForTraining` in `backend/src/find-files/request-files-prompt.ts` and `uploadExpandedFileContextForTraining` in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`. This captures expanded file context via a stronger model for training data, uploading full file contents up to 50k tokens. Schema updates in `packages/bigquery/src/schema.ts` add `get-expanded-file-context-for-training` and `get-expanded-file-context-for-training-blobs` trace types.

eli5.text: The coding assistant now saves the full contents of the files it picks, so when you ask it to look at your project it can remember every line of those files for future reference rather than just the names. A stronger model scans up to 50,000 tokens of file contents and the system records both the list of files and their full contents. If you looked at this change today you'd see the assistant keeping a more complete picture of your codebase during sessions.
